pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: The web client adds a service worker that intercepts asset image GETs, caches successful responses by URL and deployment version, accepts preload and cancellation messages, and removes older CacheStorage entries during activation. Photo viewing and thumbnail components now coordinate image work through that messaging channel. A production-stack shutdown Make target was also added, while some end-to-end UI assertions were removed.

behavior_changes.description: For clients controlled by the new service worker, matching original and thumbnail asset GETs are served from a deployment-versioned browser cache when present; otherwise they are fetched and successful 200 responses are stored for later requests.
evidence: The fetch listener limits interception to matching asset original/thumbnail paths.
immichAsset checks CacheStorage by URL before fetching and stores status-200 responses.

citations.quoted_text: let response = useCache ? await cache.match(url) : undefined;

behavior_changes.description: Adjacent photo preloading now requests service-worker-managed loading through a broadcast message instead of directly creating an image load in the viewer.
evidence: The viewer sends the generated asset URL to preloadImageUrl.
The utility emits a preload message, and the worker handles that message by invoking its asset loader.

behavior_changes.description: Destroying a photo loader or thumbnail now sends a cancellation request; if the worker has a pending load under the same normalized URL, its fetch is aborted.
evidence: Both component cleanup paths send the relevant image URL to cancelImageUrl.
The worker looks up that URL in pendingLoads and aborts the associated controller.

behavior_changes.description: Operators can now stop the production Docker Compose stack and remove orphaned containers with the new prod-down Make target.
evidence: The added target invokes docker compose down against the production compose file.

important_symbols.reason: This is the central cache, network-fetch, response-storage, and cancellation-registration path for intercepted asset requests.
Activation invokes this function to delete every CacheStorage entry except the current deployment cache, making its ownership assumptions important.
This URL-keyed map is the coordination point between concurrent fetches and component cancellation messages.
These functions define the asynchronous protocol between page components and the service worker.
This changes the viewer's preload mechanism from a direct browser image request to service-worker messaging.
The action now ties thumbnail destruction to cancellation of a URL-keyed worker request.

local_risks.description: If asset responses vary by authenticated user or current permissions, caching solely by request URL can return a response created under an earlier identity without consulting the server. The cache name is deployment-scoped rather than user-scoped, and cache hits return immediately.

citations.quoted_text: let response = useCache ? await cache.match(url) : undefined;

local_risks.description: Activation deletes every cache on the origin except the current worker cache. If another feature or co-hosted application owns a CacheStorage entry, an update can destroy data outside this worker's ownership.

The worker tracks only one AbortController per URL. Concurrent loads of the same URL overwrite that slot, so one component's cleanup can abort another request, while completion of an older request can delete the newer request's tracking entry.

The cache write is started without being awaited. Worker termination or a rejected CacheStorage operation can therefore leave successful responses uncached and can surface an unhandled promise rejection rather than making cache persistence part of the handled request lifecycle.
